clauses.reason: Executive Order 10963, signed 1961-09-01, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Pullman Company and the Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul & Pacific Railroad Company and certain of their employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10963_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10963_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_a3eb3dd50c.txt) gives the date 1961-12-11 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1961-12-11, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1962-01-10, and the order was functionally spent on 1962-01-10 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16624: the number 10963 followed by the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10963 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.
